newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says construction slump to continue this year.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says construction slump to continue this year.

text.p: The slump in the German construction industry will end in 1998 at the earliest, with output and jobs in the sector continuing to fall this year, the German government said in a report on Wednesday.

The slump in the building sector, which began in 1995, is a drag on the overall economic outlook, said the report by Construction Minister Klaus Toepfer and Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt, which was approved by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet.
The decline in jobs and output should slow this year, however, with a decline of about three percent in construction investment and 100,000 jobs lost, the report said.
Tight public-sector finances, and the 1996 downturn in east German construction are the main reasons for the slump.
Another factor was employers' efforts to circumvent expensive new contracts aimed at making up for the "bad-weather bonuses" that were eliminated last year.
The government does not favour a reintroduction of the bad-weather bonuses, however. Instead, it urged employers and construction workers to agree on a winter bonus that would be acceptable to both.
The government also hopes to extend the minimum-wage legislation for the sector.

It outlined a 16-point programme to support the construction industry, including continuation of a ban on non-EU foreign workers, better controls on construction sites, and a multi-billion mark loan programme.
